source.title: A Generalizable Approach to Learning Optimizers
source.authors: Diogo Almeida; Clemens Winter; Jie Tang; W. Zaremba

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares held-out image-classification performance for AdamW and SGD under the same stated epoch counts, bearing on V4's optimizer comparison. It does not test the other claim versions.
record.gate_note: Only the ResNet ImageNet AdamW-versus-SGD comparison directly bears on V4. Other reported outcomes evaluate the learned hyperparameter optimizer against baselines, not the claim versions' named effects. Results cited from prior work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study's own ImageNet baselines compare AdamW with learning-rate- and schedule-tuned SGD at 90 epochs. Their held-out performance bears directly on V4, although evaluating learned optimizers is the paper's main purpose.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the ImageNet qualification: AdamW is a weak baseline, and the adaptive LHOPTs improve on it while remaining below SGD. The paper's broader conclusion is that learned hyperparameter optimizers transfer to substantially different tasks, with approximately 2x ImageNet and 2.5x large-language-model training speedups over the stated baselines.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates learned hyperparameter schedules and reports AdamW and SGD reference baselines; it does not reproduce the optimizer comparisons in the claim's cited sources.
record.method_sensitivity: ImageNet model architecture (Resnet18 versus Resnet50) is reported separately; both show the same direction for AdamW versus SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: Learned hyperparameter optimizers transfer to new tasks and improve performance or training speed over adaptive baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned optimizer policies can transfer across architectures, modalities, and computational scales.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix D reports larger relative test-versus-validation discrepancies for SGD than AdamW on ResNet-18, despite SGD's better held-out performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects discrepancies between tuning-validation and held-out metrics; these discrepancies are distinct from training-to-test generalization gaps and absolute held-out performance.

record.problems: The study calls AdamW a weak baseline for ResNets on ImageNet. It reports no uncertainty for the comparison, and this evidence covers only two ImageNet architectures and one epoch budget.
record.rows_left_out: Learned-optimizer results and other task benchmarks were left out because they do not measure a version's named effect. Cited prior-work results were not extracted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.

Language-benchmark adaptive-versus-SGD comparisons; equal or better adaptive training performance; whether broader conventional hyperparameter tuning removes the difference; the causal benefit of decoupling weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language-model exceptions.
Controlled batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and remedies for large-batch penalties.
Dropout effects and their dependence on training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of training-to-test generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

missing.what: Additional held-out measures corroborate the optimizer comparison: ResNet-18 AdamW versus SGD has top-5 accuracy 87.52% versus 88.62% and loss 1.39 versus 1.26; ResNet-50 has top-5 accuracy 89.66% versus 92.09% and loss 1.35 versus 1.01. These are additional measures of the same comparisons, not independent replications.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. Its AdamW comparison supports the limited-tuning result, but does not isolate the effect of decoupled weight decay or establish that AdamW had equal or better training performance. Learned-optimizer method comparisons do not by themselves test the claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Language benchmarks; limited hyperparameter tuning as a general condition; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models.
Dropout, training-set-size regimes, and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: Resnet18 + AdamW
rows.operation_detail: Trained on ImageNet with AdamW for 90 epochs; compared with a tuned SGD baseline.
rows.note: AdamW had lower Acc@1 than the SGD comparator.
rows.check: The numbers are correct, but the state should be observed: AdamW's 67.32% accuracy is below SGD's 69.10%, as V4 predicts. Evaluation uses the half of ImageNet's validation set reserved from tuning.

rows.note: AdamW had lower Acc@1 than the SGD comparator.
rows.check: The numbers are correct, but the state should be observed: AdamW's 71.42% accuracy is below SGD's 74.66%, as V4 predicts. Evaluation uses the half of ImageNet's validation set reserved from tuning.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18 and ResNet-50 on ImageNet, 90 epochs, with learning-rate and schedule tuning
relationships.reason: R1 and R2 show AdamW trailing SGD by 1.78 and 3.24 accuracy percentage points, respectively; no uncertainty is reported.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower AdamW accuracy than SGD after learning-rate and schedule tuning remains unverified, with no uncertainty reported.
